scope: Sitara and mmWave families: AM13 (AM13E230x), Sitara MCUs AM26x (AM263, AM263P, AM261, AM273x) and AM24x (AM243x), K3 Linux processors (AM62x, AM62A, AM62P, AM62L, AM64x, TDA4VM) and the mmWave radar sensors (IWR6843, IWR6843AOP, AWR6843, IWRL6432, AWRL6432, AWR2944 family). Research only; no board was connected, flashed or reset. Sources: CCStudio 21.0.1 targetdb, GEL and DebugServer flashDB/propertyDB; UniFlash 9.6.0 (DSLite, FlashDLLDB, sitara_mcu and mmWave Python programmers); xPack OpenOCD 0.12.0-7 and TI's OpenOCD fork scripts and the am13e230x.c driver; AM13E230x SDK 26.01.00.03 docs; datasheets SPRSPC3A, SPRSP81E, SPRSP74F, SPRSPA7C, SWRS245D, SPRSP65J, SPRSP58C, SPRSP77E, SPRSP89E, SPRSPA1B, SPRSP56J, SPRSP36L, SWRS219F, SWRS248E, SWRS237C, SWRS298B, SWRS323B; TRMs SPRUJ55D, SPRUJ17I, SPRUJB6B, SPRUIU0E, SPRUIM2J, SPRUIV7C, SPRUJ16C, SPRUJ83E, SPRUJB4A, SPRUIL1D; repo measured facts by path. 'unknown' means no file read answers it. The AM263P board is returned; its notes are history.

probe_sequence.do: Read what the probe is (XDS110 on a LaunchPad or EVM, external XDS110/XDS200). Do not pick a tool by the user's word.

Try JTAG and read the TAP IDCODE. Mask 0x0FFFFFFF. 0x0BB3802F AM64x/AM243x; 0x0BB7E02F AM62x; 0x0BB8D02F AM62A; 0x0BB9D02F AM62P; 0x0BBA702F AM62L; 0x0BB6402F TDA4VM (J721E); 0x0BB7D02F AM263x; 0x0BB9502F AM263P; 0x0BBA602F AM261x; 0x0BB6A02F AM273x; 0x0BB8902F IWRL6432. AM13 answers with the Arm DAP IDCODE 0x6BA00477 and needs the DEVICEID read.
probe_sequence.source: xPack OpenOCD 0.12.0-7 scripts/target/ti_k3.cfg; ti_am13e230x.cfg; TRMs Table 1-3; iwrl6432boost/README.md

probe_sequence.do: Read the family's device-ID register to get the member: AM26x 0x50D80038; K3 0x43000018 (JTAGID at 0x43000014); AM13 0x60111004 and 0x6011101C. Mask as in each identify entry.
No JTAG answer and a serial port: try the ROM. AM26x and K3 print 'C' at 115200 in UART boot mode; mmWave answers the 0xAA/0x20 ping in flashing mode; AM13 answers the BSL.

Write: AM13 through OpenOCD (TI fork) or DSLite or ti-bsl; AM26x and AM24x through DSLite (JTAG flasher) or the UART flasher; K3 by writing the SD card or going by UART or DFU boot to U-Boot; mmWave only through UniFlash or arprog over the serial port.

families.members_note: Names and sizes: SPRSPC3A Table 4-1. Table 7-3 lists PARTNUM 0x0BBE once beside all three rows, so the datasheet does not give a per-member PARTNUM; the flash size comes from the SRAMFLASH factory word. CCStudio carries one device file per member (AM13E23017/18/19.xml) with flash database AM13E2x_128KB/256KB/512KB. The jtag_idcode is the Arm DAP IDCODE the TI OpenOCD config expects; it is Arm's value, not unique to TI.

debug_port.protocol: JTAG (4-pin, IR length 4) into an Arm CoreSight DAP; CCStudio file names the router CS_DAP and a SEC_AP
debug_port.access: XDS110 (LaunchPad onboard, USB 0451:bef3). CCStudio default connection TIXDS110_Connection.xml. DSLite and TI's OpenOCD fork both reach the M33. CCStudio exposes an optional SWD password (AM13XSWDPassword0..3) and the datasheet lists JTAGLOCK.
debug_port.notes: If the debugger cannot connect, hold BSL_INVOKE high through power-on reset, then send FactoryReset or MassErase over the DSSM mailbox (GEL) or the BSL. TI's board file runs the XDS110 at 10 MHz.

write_paths.detail: TI's OpenOCD fork (target/ti_am13e230x.cfg, driver `am13`, banks main at 0x00000000 and nonmain at 0x60100000, 0x800-byte sectors, 128-bit ECC program). frl writes main flash this way today; a 512 kB dump plus NONMAIN took 6.7 s without halting the core (E216). xPack OpenOCD 0.12.0-7 has no am13e230x file. The research note of 2026-10-18 says upstream OpenOCD master has it; not checked here.

write_paths.detail: libFlashAM13E2x.dylib with flash database AM13E2x_{128,256,512}KB. Properties: Erase and Program / Program Only / Verify Only; erase Necessary Banks / Entire Flash / Bank 0 / Bank 1; CMDWEPROTA/B sector write protection; 'Program Non-Main Flash' toggle (default off, warns an incorrect Non-Main field can brick the device); range avoidance; checksum. The FlashDLLDB.xml in UniFlash 9.6.0 has no AM13 line, so the AM13 flash path is reached through the device file's FlashDB property, not the part-number table.

write_paths.detail: ti-bsl (TI BSL Toolkit, Python 3.12+ wheel in SDK tools/am13e230x): info, read, mass-erase, range erase, flash firmware, factory reset (erases NONMAIN and MAIN, reprograms NONMAIN), change baud, start application. UART over a serial port on Windows, Linux and macOS; I2C needs an FT232H. A blank device invokes the BSL by itself. Password file needed for protected operations.
write_paths.source: AM13E230x SDK 26.01.00.03 docs user_guide/chapters/tools_and_utilities/bsl_toolkit_am13e230x.md; SPRSPC3A section 7.11, Table 7-8; not run here

never_write.why: Holds boot, BSL and debug-lock configuration. A wrong field can brick the part (CCStudio warning text). Only factory reset reprograms it.
never_write.source: TI fork am13e230x.c (AM13_FLASH_BASE_NONMAIN, AM13_NONMAIN_SIZE_PER_BANK); AM13E2x_512KB_FlashProperties.xml FlashNonMainWarningText; data/routes.json never_write

never_write.range: 0x60111000 and up (TRACEID, DEVICEID, USERID, SRAMFLASH, trim)
never_write.why: Read-only factory data and trim; not a write target.
The program command generates ECC itself (PROGRAM_128_WITH_ECC); writing it by hand breaks reads.
never_write.source: TI fork am13e230x.c AM13_PROGRAM_128_BYTEN; data/routes.json never_write

never_write.why: Factory reset erases NONMAIN and MAIN and rewrites NONMAIN. Use only to recover a locked part, with owner approval.

boot_mode.pins: No boot-mode strap. BSL_INVOKE pin high (level set in NONMAIN) at reset invokes the BSL; a blank part (no reset vector or stack pointer) invokes it automatically; the application can invoke it by SYSRST. LaunchPad: populate jumper J11 and press BSL_INV.

recovery.symptom: Debugger cannot connect to the M33, or stuck after 'Attempting CS_DAP Connection'
recovery.fix: Pull BSL_INVOKE high (LaunchPad: J11 populated, press BSL_INV), power-on reset, keep it high, issue FactoryReset or MassErase through the DSSM GEL commands. This erases the part: owner approval only.
BSL over UART (ti-bsl) writes it without a debugger; a blank part invokes the BSL on its own.

families.backup_restore: Back up: OpenOCD dump_image of main flash (512 kB) and NONMAIN (E216: 6.7 s, identical to the motor lane's image) or `ti-bsl read` for the readable regions. Restore: OpenOCD flash write with sector erase of main flash. Do not restore NONMAIN unless a factory reset forces it.

write_paths.detail: UniFlash 9.6.0 / CCStudio DSLite, flash library libFlashSitaraMCU.dylib (FlashDLLDB: JTAG, TMS470RDX, part numbers beginning AM2). DSLite loads TI's flasher program over JTAG into R5F RAM (ccs_base/sitara_mcu/flasher/: am263x, am263px_cc, am263px_lp, am263px_sip, am261x_lp, am261x_som, am243x_alv, am243x_alx, am273x). Choose board (CC or LP), part (Standard or SIP) or a custom flasher .out. Images and addresses in the device file: SBL 0x60000000, application 0x60081000 (AM263P, AM261x) or 0x60080000 (AM263x, AM273x), XIP 0xE0000000, HSM runtime 0x60040000. Erase: entire flash or a sector list.
write_paths.source: ccs_base/DebugServer/bin/FlashDLLDB.xml; ccs_base/DebugServer/propertyDB/AM263Px_FlashProperties.xml; CCStudio 21.0.1 ccs_base/common/targetdb/devices/AM263Px.xml, AM263x.xml, AM261x.xml, am273x.xml; Mac use on AM263P recorded in am263p/AGENTS.md (history)

write_paths.detail: UART flash: set boot pins to UART, open UART0 at 115200, send TI's flasher .tiimage by XMODEM-1K, then each file with a header (magic 'BLUF', operation 0xF0 flash, 0xF1 flash+verify, 0xF2/0xF3 XIP, 0xF8/0xF9 MCELF XIP, 0xFE erase). The same protocol is in the MCU+ SDK `tools/boot/uart_uniflash.py` (SDK not installed on this Mac). Application offset must be non-zero and 128 kB aligned. The protocol has verify but no read command: no backup by UART.
write_paths.source: UniFlash 9.6.0 sitara_mcu/serial/FlashPython.py and FlashPythonUtils.py; CCStudio 21.0.1 ccs_base/common/targetdb/devices/AM263Px_Serial.xml, AM261x_Serial.xml, AM273x_Serial.xml; docs/research/open-flash-path-by-family-2026-10-18.md (uart_uniflash.py)

write_paths.detail: Debug, load to RAM and run only: ti_k3.cfg declares no flash bank. TI's board files cover LP-AM263, LP-AM263P, LP-AM261, AM273x. Flash writing through OpenOCD would mean loading TI's flasher by hand: not tried.

never_write.range: 0x0 to the application offset: SBL at 0x0 (flash offset; CCStudio address 0x60000000)
never_write.why: The ROM loads the SBL from flash. Erasing it sends the ROM to its UART fallback (OSPI/QSPI modes) or to nothing. Rewrite only with a known-good .tiimage.

never_write.why: The HSM runs it at boot. Treat as part of the boot chain; write only with TI's .hsmimage.bin.

never_write.region: OSPI PHY tuning pattern sector (AM263P board, measured)
never_write.range: 4 kB sector at flash offset 0x80000, just below the AM263P application image at 0x81000
never_write.why: TI's flash driver erases and writes it when PHY tuning fails to read back. A backup that skips it loses a block.
One-time programmable; not part of any flash path.

boot_mode.pins: SOP[3:0] sampled at PORz release: SPI0_D0 (SOP3), SPI0_CLK (SOP2), OSPI0_D1/QSPI_D1 (SOP1), OSPI0_D0/QSPI_D0 (SOP0). AM263P: 0000 OSPI 4S, 0001 UART, 0010 OSPI 1S, 0011 OSPI 8S, 1011 DevBoot, 1100 xSPI 8D (SFDP). AM263x: 0000 QSPI 4S, 0001 UART, 0010 QSPI 1S, 0100 QSPI 4S with UART fallback, 0101 QSPI 1S with UART fallback, 1011 DevBoot. AM261x: AM263P list plus 1110 USB DFU. AM273x: SOP_MODE4 QSPI, SOP_MODE5 UART, SOP_MODE6 SBL development, set on PMIC_OUT, SYNC_OUT and TDO. The AM263P OSPI modes fall back to UART on failure. LP-AM263P boot switch SW1 positions 1 and 2 ON, 3 and 4 OFF is the OSPI setting by photo (history).
boot_mode.source: TRM SPRUJ55D Table 5-1 and 5-2; SPRUJ17I Table 5-2; SPRUJB6B Table 5-2; SPRUIU0E Table 5-2; am263p/README.md

recovery.symptom: SBL erased or corrupt, OSPI boot fails
recovery.fix: Set the boot pins to UART (0001, AM273x SOP_MODE5), power cycle, send the flasher and SBL again by UART or DSLite. The ROM cannot be damaged.
recovery.source: TRM SPRUJ55D Table 5-1; UniFlash sitara_mcu FlashPython.py

recovery.fix: Plug the USB-C supply (micro-B feeds only the probe); delete a copied 'SWD Mode' property from the connection file.

recovery.symptom: Memory window at 0x60000000 reads one byte value throughout
recovery.fix: The flash controller is not set up. A read-only backup needs a program or the ROM boot to have opened the flash first; opening can rewrite sector 0x80000, so read the sector first.
Power cycle the board and run again.

families.backup_restore: These parts have no flash inside (except the AM263P ZCZ-F in-package flash on its OSPI bus). Back up = read the OSPI window at 0x60000000 over JTAG with DSLite `memory` (8 reads of 4 MB, twice, compare); worked on the AM263P with caveats (needs the controller opened; the upper 16 MB mirrored the lower; history). Restore = DSLite flash with the same bytes at the same offsets, or UART flash with verify. The UART path cannot read back.

probe.bare_chip: 20-pin cTI JTAG from an XDS110 or XDS200; UART0 plus the four SOP straps and nRESET for ROM boot.

write_paths.detail: The program is the boot medium: an SD card (MMCSD boot, FAT with tiboot3.bin, tispl.bin, u-boot.img, then a Linux image). Write TI's .wic image to the card (`xz -dc IMAGE | sudo dd of=/dev/rdiskN bs=4m` on Mac). TDA4VM: tda4/tools/write-card.sh; with no card reader, UART boot then write from the board (tda4/tools/uart_boot.py, write_from_stick.py).

UART boot: XMODEM tiboot3.bin to the ROM, then tispl.bin and u-boot.img (XMODEM or YMODEM from SPL) to reach U-Boot with no card. 115200 baud, about 11.5 kB/s; AM62L ROM times out at 5 minutes; measured 7 minutes to U-Boot on the AM62L. USB DFU boot (AM62L SW3 ON ON ON ON; AM64x/AM62x primary 1010) is far faster. From U-Boot write SD, eMMC or OSPI.
write_paths.source: am62l-evm/UART-BOOT.md; TRM SPRUJB4A Table 5-1; tda4/README.md; TI Linux SDK UART page not available here

write_paths.detail: Debug only: connect, halt, load RAM (AM62L Zephyr in SRAM was loaded this way). UniFlash 9.6.0 has no flash library for K3 Linux parts: FlashDLLDB part-number rules cover AM2* (JTAG) and AM*(Serial) but the K3 Linux device files carry no flash database or serial variant.
k3 target with board files for every K3 EVM: debug and RAM load only, no flash bank.

boot_mode.pins: BOOTMODE[15:0]: B2:B0 reference clock, B6:B3 primary boot mode, B9:B7 primary options, B12:B10 backup mode, B13 backup option. Primary B6:B3 (AM62x, AM62A, AM62P): 0001 OSPI, 0010 QSPI, 0011 SPI, 0100 Ethernet RGMII, 0101 RMII, 0110 I2C, 0111 UART, 1000 MMCSD (SD card or eMMC UDA), 1001 eMMC boot partition, 1010 USB, 1011 GPMC NAND, 1100 GPMC NOR, 1110 xSPI, 1111 no-boot/dev boot. Backup B12:B10: 001 USB, 011 UART, 100 Ethernet, 101 MMCSD, 110 SPI, 111 I2C. AM62L (reduced pincount, SW3 = BOOTMODE[15:12]): ON is 1; shipped OFF OFF OFF OFF is SD primary with full pincount; ON OFF ON OFF is SD primary, UART backup; ON ON ON OFF is UART primary, SD backup; ON ON ON ON is USB DFU primary; table values 0x007B DevBoot, 0x0D53 USB host MSC, 0x044B eMMC, 0x0C13 QSPI, 0x0E43 SD, 0x343B UART, 0x3453 USB DFU. SK-TDA4VM SW1: all OFF boots the SD card; 1 ON, 2 OFF, 3 ON, 4 OFF is UART boot. TDA4VM also has MCU_BOOTMODE pins and an MCU-only mode. Full power cycle after any change; the AM62L SW7 reset does not re-read them. Boards other than AM62L and SK-TDA4VM: switch tables not read.
boot_mode.source: TRMs SPRUIV7C Table 5-4, 5-5; SPRUJ16C and SPRUJ83E Table 5-4; SPRUIM2J Table 4-2 to 4-5; SPRUJB4A Tables 5-3, 5-5, 5-6, 5-7; SPRUIL1D Tables 4-2 to 4-9; am62l-evm/AGENTS.md; tda4/AGENTS.md

recovery.fix: Check boot switches and the serial port first; the card or eMMC may be blank. Switch to UART or DFU boot and rebuild the card from U-Boot.

recovery.symptom: AM62L: switches changed, nothing new happens
recovery.fix: Unplug and replug the main power (J17); SW7 does not re-read the pins.

recovery.symptom: UART boot sent more than 5 minutes after power gets 'receiver cancelled'
recovery.fix: Power cycle and send within the ROM window; a `reboot` from default Linux returns to the ROM ping.

recovery.symptom: Micro-SD 'Transfer data timeout' / 'Card did not respond to voltage select'
recovery.fix: Bad or unseated card; eMMC still answers. Use UART boot plus a USB stick.

families.backup_restore: Nothing programmable lives in the chip: the ROM and fuses are fixed. The 'program' is the boot medium. Back up = read the whole SD card (or eMMC) to an image file; restore = write that image back (an interrupted write is safe to rerun because chunks go to fixed block addresses, TDA4VM tool). If the card cannot be read on the Mac (no reader), reach U-Boot by UART boot and use `ums` or a USB stick as the bridge. A box-shipped card was never read back on this bench, so the factory content is only recoverable from TI's published image.

write_paths.detail: UniFlash 9.6.0 'Flash Only' serial programmer (FlashPython), selected by part-number prefix AWR, IWR, AR, IR. Four Python generations are bundled: gen1 for xWR12, xWR14, xWR16, xWR18, xWR68 (IWR6843, IWR6843AOP, AWR6843): meta images 1 to 4 in .bin; gen3 for xWRL64 and xWRL14 (IWRL6432, AWRL6432): .appimage or .bin; gen4 for xWRL68 (IWRL6844, AWRL6844); gen2 for the SBL-plus-app parts (AWR2944, AWR2x44P, AWR2544: SBL image and app image, sbl_uart_uniflash.release.tiimage, app offset 0xA0000; gen2 mapping is inferred from the matching image types and offset). Protocol: SOP pins to flashing mode, serial 115200, sync 0xAA, START_DOWNLOAD 0x21, SEND_DATA 0x24, FILE_CLOSE 0x22, ERASE 0x28 (storages SDRAM 0, FLASH 1, SFLASH 2, EEPROM 3, SRAM 4). Option 'Format' or erase-before-download wipes the whole SFLASH. UniFlash adds a CONFIG file (ar1xxx_config.bin) to xWR68 downloads automatically. No opcode reads flash back.
write_paths.source: UniFlash 9.6.0 ccs_base/mmWave/gen1..gen4/FlashPython.py and mmWaveProgFlash.py; FlashDLLDB.xml; CCStudio 21.0.1 ccs_base/common/targetdb/devices/iwr6843.xml, iwrl6432.xml, awr2944.xml, awr2544.xml

boot_mode.pins: xWR68xx (IWR6843, IWR6843AOP, AWR6843): SOP2:SOP1:SOP0 = 001 functional (loads the application from QSPI flash into RAM), 101 flashing (UART), 011 debug (R4F halted). xWRL64xx (IWRL6432): SOP1:SOP0 = 01 functional, 00 flashing, 11 debug (M4F halted). IWRL6432BOOST S1: positions 1 and 2 are SOP0 and SOP1; SOP0 ON and SOP1 OFF is application mode; S1 position 1 OFF plus S2 (NRST) is flashing. Pins are shared with TDO (SOP0), SYNC_OUT (SOP1), PMIC_CLKOUT (SOP2) on 68xx and with TDO and PMIC_CLKOUT on L6432.
boot_mode.source: SWRS219F Table 8-1; SWRS248E Table 8-1; SWRS237C Table 8-1; SWRS298B Table 8-3, Table 6-3, Table 6-7; SWRS323B Table 8-3; iwrl6432boost/AGENTS.md

recovery.fix: Put the board in flashing mode first (S1 position 1 OFF, press S2) and wait for 2 s of silence.

recovery.symptom: 'Initial response from the device was not received. Please power cycle device before re-flashing.'
recovery.fix: Power cycle with the SOP straps in flashing mode, run again.

recovery.symptom: Application will not run after a failed or partial flash
recovery.fix: The ROM bootloader is untouched: set flashing mode and write the meta images (application and firmware patch) again.

families.backup_restore: No tested backup. The serial bootloader has no read command, and no tool was found that reads the radar's serial flash back, so the shipped image cannot be saved (iwrl6432boost/AGENTS.md, RD1). The cycle for these parts is therefore: record the image you flash, write it, check by running it (demo output on the data port, or the ROM's per-file status), and restore by writing the known-good .appimage or meta images again. A factory restore uses TI's prebuilt image from Radar Toolbox (a candidate for the BOOST: Motion and Presence 2D image; whether it equals the shipped one is unknown).
